correctness.rationale: The row-column count identity (1) is exact. Two-colourings correspond to sign solutions of row/column balance equations, and all cases a,b>=2 are exhausted. Modulo-three colouring works by a proved global ceiling inequality for a+b>=14, by a finite check of all smaller a,b, and by two displayed finite exception matrices. The 4-colour modular construction covers the two genuine three-colour obstructions. For K_(3,4), a counting bound forces three classes of four edges each, each necessarily K_(2,2), incompatible with odd column degrees. For K_(4,5), exhaustive vertex-degree cases give six edges maximum per colour class, so three colours cover at most eighteen of twenty edges. The standalone script was executed successfully from its standalone packaged source and exhaustively checked all 2^20 one-class subsets for that finite exceptional case. No finite experiment substitutes for the infinite part.

value.rationale: A complete classification of a natural two-parameter family identifies the genuine low-degree four-colour boundary and combines explicit optimal constructions with an exact parity rigidity theorem for all two-colour solutions. The previously known K_(4,5) obstruction is contextual, while K_(3,4) and all low-degree strips are determined uniformly rather than as arbitrary numerical table entries. These sharpen general statements whose degree conditions leave infinitely many bicliques unresolved. The counting structure and extremal obstruction are motivated by the strong-majority edge index, not an artificial parameter specialization.
